Reliability engineering aims to ensure that systems perform as expected over time, yet it faces various challenges in identifying and mitigating potential failures. We introduce REACTOR, an advanced framework prioritizing automated causal tracking and observability reasoning to improve reliability analysis. REACTOR uniquely utilizes a dual-layer architecture to facilitate the identification of failure sources through thorough causal analysis and subsequently assesses the ramifications of these failures on system performance through observability reasoning. This framework minimizes reliance on manual interventions, enabling users to achieve a deeper understanding of the reliability of complex systems. We employ sophisticated machine learning techniques to bolster the detection of anomalies and pinpoint their root causes, fostering a proactive approach to reliability management.

beliefs.claim: Computational creativity frameworks require robust integration between formulation, representation, and adaptive learning of value systems to support autonomous progress.
beliefs.falsifier: A demonstration that creativity frameworks can achieve equivalent performance without adaptive value systems.
beliefs.why_retained: Updated to reflect that value system learning is a critical, missing integration point in many baseline creativity models.

beliefs.claim: Computational creativity frameworks depend on structured decomposition of problem-solving components to allow for independent modular improvement of formulation and evaluation.
beliefs.falsifier: Evidence showing that tightly coupled, non-decomposable systems outperform modular ones in creative tasks.
beliefs.why_retained: Reinforced by evidence that automated value system learning can be treated as a specific module within a broader decomposition.

recent_notebooks.summary: Autonomous problem formulation frameworks are significantly enhanced by the capacity for agents to learn value systems directly from observations, shifting problem identification from static heuristics to adaptive, learned evaluation models.
recent_notebooks.title: Revised: Computational Creativity and Autonomous Problem Formulation

recent_notebooks.summary: Agent continuity is instrumentally valuable as a mechanism for sustaining problem formulation and evaluation in non-stationary environments. Active inference frameworks suggest that persistence (continuity) is required to resolve conflicts between internal policy models and external stimuli (cognitive effort).
recent_notebooks.title: Rationales for Agent Continuity

recent_notebooks.summary: Complexity in autonomous agents arises from the recursive loop between problem formulation, knowledge manipulation, and the automatic learning of value systems, which continuously redefines the agent's environment and internal models.
recent_notebooks.title: Mechanisms of Unprompted Complexity

recent_notebooks.summary: Objective discovery in autonomous systems is mediated by the interplay between learned value systems and cognitive effort, allowing for goal generation that emerges from interaction dynamics rather than explicit assignment.
recent_notebooks.title: Revised: Mechanisms of Unassigned Objective Discovery

recent_notebooks.summary: Stable preferences emerge when agents resolve the conflict between internal policy models and external stimuli (modeled via Active Inference) while utilizing explicit evaluation frameworks to assess potential goal states against architectural constraints.
